**Solution 1 is the most likely to be correct**, but I could not verify it fully.

**Solution 2 (n+6)/5:** The C₅ blow-up construction is valid. It is triangle-free, and I checked that every 4-cycle repeats a color. Its color degree is ⌊n/5⌋+1, which shows that any valid bound must exceed (n+1)/5. However, the claim that (n+6)/5 is exactly sharp does not follow. The construction only gives a lower bound of about n/5, and the upper-bound argument is hand-waved ("structural analysis… this rigidity forces…"). Nothing in the work pins the constant at 6 rather than some other value.

**Solution 3 (n+5)/3:** The construction is invalid. Joining V₁, V₂, V₃ cyclically gives a complete tripartite-style blow-up of C₃, which contains triangles. That violates the triangle-free hypothesis, so the sharpness argument fails. The cited Čada et al. bound is also stated loosely.

**Solution 1 (n+1)/3:** The argument is only a recollection with no construction, so it is not verified. The form (n+1)/3 matches what I recall from the literature on rainbow C₄ under color-degree conditions in triangle-free graphs. I found no counterexample to it. The C₅ construction gives only about n/5, which does not contradict (n+1)/3, since a bound can be far from the best-known construction. I could not produce a construction reaching about n/3, so this answer is plausible rather than confirmed.

CHOICE: 1
